title: Explant Selection and Surface Disinfection
objective: Select explants and design surface-disinfection trials that reduce external contamination without destroying viable tissue.

terms.definition: A controlled treatment intended to reduce microorganisms on exposed tissue surfaces; it does not establish sterility inside the plant.
A microorganism living within plant tissue without necessarily producing visible symptoms.
Movement or manipulation of culture material using practices intended to prevent introduction of unwanted microorganisms.
Damage to cultured plant tissue caused by cutting, handling, chemical exposure, temperature, or other treatment.
The proportion of cultures showing defined contamination within a stated observation interval.
Pre-culture management and documentation of source plants intended to improve explant quality and reduce contamination risk before collection.

coreScience: Surface disinfection targets organisms on exposed tissue surfaces. It does not reliably eliminate internal endophytes or systemic pathogens. Cannabis nodal explants can carry internal contaminants that emerge after apparently successful surface treatment.
Explant type, age, source position, donor-room sanitation, preconditioning, chemical identity, concentration, exposure, agitation, rinse quality, and operator technique all influence establishment.
More aggressive treatment can reduce contamination while also damaging meristems, leaves, and axillary buds. The useful protocol balances viable clean establishment against tissue injury.
cultivationRelevance: Improve donor cleanliness before increasing chemical severity. Run small controlled trials, include untreated or current-standard comparisons when appropriate, and identify contaminants rather than assuming every cloudy culture has the same cause.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Donor and explant; prewash; agent and concentration; exposure and rinse; operator; contamination type and day detected; tissue survival; shoot recovery.

For explant selection and surface disinfection, record the relevant developmental stage, environment, operator or treatment condition, and time sequence so the biological response can be separated from handling and facility effects.

Record the defined success endpoint, failures and off-types, replicate or batch variation, and any identity, health, rooting, survival, or follow-up test used to verify that the apparent result persisted after establishment.

misconceptions: Bleach sterilizes the inside of the plant. Visible similarity alone does not prove equivalent physiological state, health status, or later performance; identity and outcome measurements answer different questions.

Stronger surface treatment is always better. A single observation or negative symptom check cannot exclude latent infection, developmental history, or protocol-specific effects; use the appropriate follow-up test or repeated observation.

A clear vessel after a few days proves a clean culture. Cultivar names, appearance, and one successful batch are not substitutes for traceable identity, controlled comparison, and repeatable propagation outcomes.
evidenceLimits: Disinfection recipes are organism-, tissue-, genotype-, product-, and facility-specific. This lesson does not authorize a chemical, concentration, contact time, rinse sequence, PPE set, or product use. Current product labeling, chemical-safety controls, and facility procedures govern actual use.
